//: Handbook §26 delivery gate, point 3: numeric floors for mobile performance and accessibility. A threshold with no job that runs it produces the same software as no threshold, so these are merge conditions rather than aspirations.
//measured: Set on 2026-08-12 from the median of three CI runs, not guessed: performance 64, accessibility 97, best-practices 100, SEO 100, LCP 6.8s, CLS 0, TBT 10ms.
//headroom: Each floor sits below the measured score by about the run-to-run variance Lighthouse shows on a shared runner. A floor set flush against today's number goes red on noise, and a gate that cries wolf is a gate somebody removes - which is the failure this whole adoption is written against. Raise them as the scores improve; that is the ratchet idea applied to a number instead of a count.
//performance: 0.55 against a measured 64 is the loosest floor here, and deliberately so: LCP is 6.8s and the largest remaining cause is the render-blocking Google Fonts stylesheet on a third-party origin. That is DEBT-04, which is also a privacy finding - the same fix moves both. Tighten this to 0.75 in the commit that self-hosts the typefaces.

assertions.//layout-shift: Measured 0 after width/height landed on all 27 images. This locks that in: it is the one metric here that is currently perfect and the easiest to lose by accident.
assertions.//blocking: Measured 10ms. 500 is generous, because the point is catching a script that starts blocking the main thread, not policing normal variation.
assertions.//lcp: Warning rather than error, and this is the honest place for it. 6.8s fails any reasonable floor already, so asserting on it would make the gate permanently red - the exact thing the ratchet exists to prevent elsewhere. It warns so the number stays in view, and it becomes an error when DEBT-04 removes the render-blocking third-party stylesheet.
